statement: The runs context captures the journal well, but it mixes three concerns: the journal of a run, machine ownership, and admission control. It also has too many writes per effect for the hot path. The rule I want everyone to accept: an effect is fenced by appending its decision to the run stream at the expected version before it is performed. Effects on our own state (files, triggers, schedules, artifacts, sqlite) commit in the same append as their result and are exactly-once. External effects (Post, Fetch, model completions) are at-least-once or in-doubt, and the effect's interface declares which. Separately, an agent turn is a run, and Sleep is a suspension of the run, not a schedule.

renames.why: the event must carry an occurrence id (schedule id + due instant), so two machines or a restart never fire the same occurrence twice; 'fired' alone hides that a cron fires many distinct occurrences

merges.why: gates are pure, so request and decision are one fact. Appending it at the expected stream version before performing is the in-doubt marker and the fence in one write. A performed effect then costs two appends (EffectPermitted, EffectResultRecorded); a mocked or denied one costs a single append (EffectMocked, EffectDenied or GateFailed). Every decision event carries label, input CID, shell CID and the rewritten input CID

splits.why: an inbound chat message (deduplicated by platform message id, starts a turn) and an outbound Post (the result of an effect, carrying run id + step as the idempotency key used for reconciliation) have opposite delivery guarantees and must not share a name

missing.why: group commit for Now, Random, Flip and the reference pins resolved since the last flush. They are buffered and appended in one event just before the next externally visible effect or state change. If the machine crashes before the flush, nobody saw those values, so re-executing them is safe

an infrastructure failure of an idempotent effect (timeout, 5xx) is retried with backoff and the same idempotency key. The retry is a durable timer on the run, not a program-visible Error, and the audit should show the attempts

Delegate, Dataclip and the agent's run tool start a child run keyed by parent run + step. Recording the link makes those effects exactly-once inside the cloud: after a crash the parent finds the existing child run instead of starting a second one

remove.why: heartbeats every few seconds would swamp the audit log and say nothing about the domain. Renewals live in the lease store; only acquisition, expiry and handover are events

moves.why: it is the session's queue of messages waiting for the next turn, not part of a program run's journal

context_changes.change: split runs into 'runs' (the journal: RunStarted .. RunCompleted, effect decisions and results, suspensions, checkpoints, divergence) and 'fleet' (MachineJoined, MachineDrained, RunLeaseAcquired, RunLeaseExpired, RunThrottled)
context_changes.why: the journal is the aggregate and the evidence. Ownership and admission are coordination, with their own lifecycle and much higher churn. Correctness must not depend on the lease, because GC pauses and partitions happen; it depends on the conditional append to the run stream. The lease only avoids wasted work

context_changes.change: an agent turn is a run: AgentTurnStarted/AgentTurnCompleted open and close a run of kind 'turn' in the runs journal. ModelResponseReceived is that run's effect result (a Complete effect); ToolCallExecuted is a ChildRunAwaited. The conversations context keeps messages, the queue and the history projection
context_changes.why: model completions are the slowest, most expensive and least deterministic effect. If a turn is not journaled, a crash mid-turn re-bills the model and can redo a tool call that already posted. One mechanism for replay instead of two

context_changes.change: schedules only delivers messages to sessions (Cron and Timeout effects, configured crons). Sleep inside a program becomes RunSuspended with a wake time owned by the run; undo the merge of TimerArmed into schedules.ScheduleRegistered
context_changes.why: a sleeping run must release its process and lease and wake on any machine. A schedule outlives the run that created it and is cancelled by name. Today Sleep is process.sleep, which pins a BEAM process for the whole wait

hotspot_positions.position: Separate events, because they have different write cost and different follow-ups. EffectPermitted (merged with EffectRequested) is followed by a result. EffectMocked carries the decision and the mocked value in one append. EffectDenied and GateFailed are terminal and followed by RunFailed, because an Unavailable effect ends the run in execute.loop today. All of them carry the shell CID, the input CID and the rewritten input CID.

Replayed steps use the recorded decisions and results: those effects already happened in the world, and checking them again cannot undo them. Replay performs nothing and evaluates no gates. Every new step after the journal head is decided against the shell that is current at resume, and the decision event records that shell CID. So a revoked permission makes the next step fail normally, and replay never extends an old Pass to new actions. If a revocation must stop in-flight runs immediately, the command that changes the shell emits RunCancelled for the runs it affects. If the next effect the replay asks for differs from the recorded one, the run gets ReplayDiverged and fails. It is never patched.

Each effect interface declares a delivery class. pure (Hash, DecodeJson): not journaled, re-executed. internal (files, triggers, schedules, artifacts, sqlite, Delegate/Dataclip child runs): the state change and EffectResultRecorded commit in one append, so they are exactly-once. idempotent external (GET Fetch, Events): retried. keyed external (Post): sent with run id + step in message metadata, and an in-doubt Post is reconciled by searching recent channel history for that key. unsafe external (non-GET Fetch, model completion): EffectOutcomeInDoubt fails the run by default and says so in the channel. A person, or a per-effect policy option such as 'retry_in_doubt: True', can choose to retry or treat it as done; either choice is recorded as EffectReconciled.

Not every result is fsynced. Pure effects are not journaled. Now, Random, Flip and the reference pins are buffered and flushed as LocalEffectResultsRecorded, in the same append as the next EffectPermitted of an externally visible or state-changing effect. ReadFile records only the root CID it read from and the result CID; the bytes are already in the block store. That gives one durable write before each visible effect and none for pure evaluation. A program that never leaves pure land and local effects costs zero writes until RunCompleted.

EffectMocked is its own event type, never an EffectResultRecorded with a flag. Replay feeds the mocked value from EffectMocked. Projections of what happened in the world (messages posted, files written, artifacts) consume only EffectResultRecorded and the internal domain events, so a mock can never show up in them.

Effect inputs and results above a small inline size are encrypted blobs referenced by CID, with keys per workspace or per subject, and erasure destroys the key. A completed run whose blobs were shredded can still be audited by its envelope but cannot be replayed, which is acceptable. An in-flight run that hits a shredded blob fails with ReplayDiverged('erased').

Each run is its own stream, and order within it is the stream version, which is also the fence. The store assigns a global position at commit for projections; no node's wall clock is authoritative for order. Results of the Now effect are data, not ordering. Each stream is hash chained, and the periodic signed checkpoint covers the global position.
Agree. Spans stay an observability view, keyed by run id + step so a trace can link to the journal, but they are sampled and lossy and never the record.

The Secret effect result is journaled as the secret's id and version, never its value, and replay reads that version from the secrets store. The proxy injects network secrets after the program, so the journaled Fetch request already contains only the placeholder. A response body that echoes a token cannot be detected reliably, so effect result blobs are encrypted (see H6) rather than redacted. SetSecret is a configuration command whose event records only that a secret was set.

References are resolved lazily (UndefinedReference breaks mid-run), so pins are recorded as they happen and flushed with LocalEffectResultsRecorded. ReferencesPinned at start covers what static analysis of the source finds. Replay never consults the hub for names, only for CIDs.

Blobs referenced by the stream of a run that is in flight or retained are roots. Compacting a completed run to RunCompleted plus its outputs releases its intermediate blobs, unless an audit hold or retention policy keeps them.

A runtime AddTrigger is an internal effect: TriggerAdded commits in the same append as its EffectResultRecorded, so it survives restarts. If a configured trigger and a runtime trigger have the same name, the configured one wins and the runtime one is reported as shadowed.

Store each delivery as a blob in the connection's stream, with retention, and dedupe by delivery id. Pattern matching is pure and cheap and runs on every delivery. Only a match produces TriggerMatched, and the run it starts is keyed by trigger + event id, so starting it is exactly-once. Matched runs pass through admission control (RunThrottled means queued, never dropped), so a burst delays scripts instead of losing them or spawning thousands of processes.

Databases are not projections; rebuilding them is too costly. A sqlite write effect runs in a transaction that also inserts (run_id, step) into a cloud-owned table. EffectResultRecorded is appended after the commit, and an in-doubt write is reconciled by checking that table, which makes sqlite writes exactly-once. DatabaseSnapshotTaken gives restore points.

Each schedule declares its catch-up policy in config. The default fires one occurrence, the latest missed, marked late, and records CronOccurrenceMissed for the skipped ones. Each workspace's scheduler is a single leased owner, and firing is idempotent on the occurrence id. Timeouts store an absolute due time, so after a restart an overdue timeout fires once, immediately.
Reverting a configuration changes only decisions made after the revert, including new steps of in-flight runs (see H2). Effects already performed stay facts, and nothing is compensated automatically.

RunStarted carries the on_behalf_of chain (person -> agent turn -> trigger/schedule). Child runs inherit it and append themselves, so every effect event can be attributed by its run without repeating the chain.

new_hotspots.text: Fencing needs the event store to support appends conditional on each run stream's version. Without that, a paused former owner and a new owner can both append and perform. Is per-stream optimistic concurrency a hard requirement for the store choice?

Continuations cannot be serialized today (closures flatten when copied between processes, see notes/cloud-process-boundaries.md), so RunCheckpointed is aspirational and replay time grows with the length of the journal. Until free-variable capture of the interpreter environment works, do we cap journal length and make long loops and repeating crons 'continue as new' (start a fresh run that carries over its state)?

A turn crashes after a tool call posted but before the next completion. Resuming from the journal reuses the recorded completions and finishes the turn; restarting the turn would post again. Do we always resume, and how does that interact with inputs queued during the crash and with /new, which must cancel the in-flight turn run?

Backpressure limits per workspace, channel and connection: how many concurrent runs, model calls and child runs are allowed, and does a Delegate count against its parent's slot (risk of deadlock when parents wait on children that cannot be admitted)?
